look_here_first: Look for LONG racemes arising in DISTINCT tiers or whorls along a flowering stem, sometimes with an upright terminal branch. The panicle can detach and tumble, but that fact and the head silhouette alone are not enough: mature spikelets should have longer awns than hooded windmillgrass, with fertile lemma awn around 4.8–9 mm and sterile lemma awn around 3.2–7 mm.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Accepted POWO species and Texas state-level native distribution; source-pool admission approved; three target-zone county confirmations not independently verified.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial windmillgrass with ~10–16 racemes in separated whorls; ripe panicle may detach and tumble.
morphology_keys.spikelets: Fertile lemma awn ~4.8–9 mm; sterile lemma awn ~3.2–7 mm. Upper sterile floret is not a conspicuously swollen round hood.
best_field_traits: Awn measurements on fertile and sterile lemmas
Upright terminal branch and sometimes intact detachable head
crew_field_walkthrough: Use the whole held seedhead and/or the botanical illustration to locate the main vertical flowering axis.
Check whether long branches arise from more than one level along the axis; in photographs, overlapping branches can hide this, so document it with a clean side-on full head.
Dissect mature spikelets and measure the fertile-lemma and sterile-lemma awns SEPARATELY; head shape alone overlaps the hybrid.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole attached flowering stalk from below lowest whorl through terminal head, with metric scale.
Same-scale matched cucullata comparison showing crowded/looser whorl separation.
Individual fertile and upper sterile florets in macro with correctly assigned awns and mm scale.
Attached mature head vs fallen detachable panicle; basal crown and leaf ligule.
morphology_keys.field_photo_limitations: Separate photo lesson can include the original USDA botanical illustration, but it must be labeled as an ILLUSTRATION, not counted as a photo or as a measured modern specimen.
crew_field_steps: On an intact stalk, photograph the entire head from the lowest tier to highest; see whether rays attach at different heights.
In the existing hand-held photograph, longer narrow lateral racemes radiate from more than one height. Fingers give a rough scale, not a millimeter measurement.
Check the mature fertile and sterile lemmas separately. Current real pictures do not resolve an awn length or a single dissection.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Tumble windmillgrass tends to have separated tiers of longer (~5–15 cm) racemes and long awns. C. cucullata tends to have crowded shorter whorls and a swollen short-awned sterile hood. C. virgata often has one terminal feathery fan and a different fertile-lemma hair crown. The hybrid between cucullata and verticillata is a real confounder: never certify hybrid status from tier spacing.
comparisons.cautions: Head color, overall windmill appearance and awn length alone can mislead. Inspect a fully mature spikelet with scale; hybrid intermediates must remain uncertain.

Dissected mature fertile and sterile lemmas with millimeter scale

Blade–sheath junction opened to show the TRUE ligule and collar with 1-mm scale; existing photographs do not show this organ.
Mature intact flowering axis photographed side-on from lowest to highest branch tier with attached stem and ruler; avoid mistaking overlapping branches for whorls.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: How to identify Chloris verticillata in the field
steps: Begin with the existing Joey Santore whole-head photograph (image 2) to recognize multiple separated flowering tiers; this CC BY-NC 4.0 image is for the noncommercial learner only.

Compare Matt Lavin's photographed branching hub (image 5): long one-sided spikelet-bearing racemes radiate from an actual junction, but this single crop does not show every tier along the complete culm.

Examine Douglas Goldman's genuine exposed fibrous-root crown (source image 8, teaching panel 6). It shows clustered flattened basal shoots and bent stems, NOT roots at an individual decumbent stem node. In living plants, follow any creeping stem to see whether a real node has rooted; do not invent a stolon/rhizome based on a bend.

Examine Goldman's blade/sheath junction (source image 9, teaching panel 7). The two arrows indicate the actual junction and visibly pale hairs. To verify the species' shortly ciliate MEMBRANOUS ligule, peel open the INNER blade/sheath junction, photograph its FREE edge next to 1-mm scale, and separate membrane from neighboring longer hairs. No current photo establishes this length.

Study Matt Lavin's source-labelled detached awned spikelets (image 4) and attached awned raceme (image 11). Awns are visible; glume versus fertile/sterile lemma identity and insertion need a measured dissection.

For species-level separation, photograph ONE authenticated local specimen from rooted base through attached tiered seedhead, including lower nodes (and rooted nodes if present), then dissect mature spikelets with a physical 1-mm scale. On C. cucullata distinguish the 1–1.5 mm UPPER GLUME from the separately inflated sterile-floret 'hood'; compare feather windmillgrass at matched scale, and never infer a hybrid from tier spacing.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Tumble windmillgrass tends to have separated tiers of longer (~5–15 cm) racemes and long awns. C. cucullata tends to have crowded shorter whorls and a swollen short-awned sterile hood. C. virgata often has one terminal feathery fan and a different fertile-lemma hair crown. The hybrid between cucullata and verticillata is a real confounder: never certify hybrid status from tier spacing.

The 11-panel comparison gallery remains unchanged except one verified collar-hair arrow. Photo indices are zero-based images[] entries. Do not claim measured glume/lemma/ligule anatomy or 100% completion from these photos; Joey CC BY-NC files remain noncommercial-use conditional.

diagnostic_species_finalization_20261024.look_here_first: On ONE intact flowering culm, find long one-sided racemes arising in well-separated tiers/whorls and a solitary upright terminal branch. Then confirm the longer upper glume and two DIFFERENT lemma awns on a mature spikelet; a detached tumblehead or whorl spacing alone is not conclusive.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261024.measured_growth_and_collar: Warm-season tufted perennial; culms about 14–40 cm (Flora of North America/Kew). Basal stems may bend and root at lower nodes, but current gallery does not prove rooted nodes. Blade commonly 2–3 mm wide. FNA: shortly ciliate membranous ligule 0.7–1.3 mm, sheath mostly hairless with hairs up to 3 mm near collar; Kew GrassBase: ciliate membrane about 2 mm. Preserve both reference ranges; never measure the ligule from a distant photograph.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261024.measured_flowering_axis: Typically 10–16 unilateral racemes, each about 5–15 cm, borne in several well-separated whorls on a central axis about 1–4 cm (Kew), commonly with one solitary upright terminal raceme (FNA). The peduncle can break above the uppermost sheath and the entire mature head may tumble; require an attached stalk to interpret the branch levels.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261024.measured_spikelet_glumes: Spikelet body about 2–3.5 mm excluding long awns (Go Botany). One lower bisexual/fertile floret plus one upper sterile floret. Lower glume about 2–3 mm; upper glume about 2.8–3.5 mm (FNA), upper glume one-veined, keeled (Kew). Both glumes are distinct from the awn-bearing lemmas; do not label a glume as the source of either long awn.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261024.measured_fertile_lemma: Lower fertile lemma about 2–3.5 mm long and 1.5–1.9 mm wide (FNA), keeled and three-veined (Kew); one subapical awn about 4.8–9 mm. Margin and keel hairs vary; don't invent hair arrows without a resolved macro.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261024.measured_sterile_lemma: Upper sterile lemma about 1.1–2.3 mm, oblong, somewhat inflated/truncate but NOT the rounded hood of C. cucullata; its midvein extends as a separate approximately 3.2–7 mm awn. Label fertile and sterile lemmas independently in an opened mature spikelet.
crew_identification_steps: 1. Trace a single rooted or attached culm from basal tuft to the whole flowering axis; photograph lower nodes and any actual adventitious roots without assuming them.
2. Count racemes on that ONE axis and mark their attachment tiers; verify a solitary upright terminal branch where present.
3. Open a real blade/sheath junction and measure the shortly ciliate membranous ligule with a 1-mm scale; do not confuse adjacent hairs with membrane length.
4. At 10–20× isolate one mature spikelet, show its one bisexual and one upper sterile floret, and measure the body excluding awns.
5. Separate lower and upper glumes and check the upper glume against 2.8–3.5 mm, not the 1–1.5 mm typical of hooded windmillgrass.
6. Follow each of the TWO long awns back to its respective fertile or upper sterile LEMMA; measure them independently.
7. Compare a same-scale mature C. cucullata spikelet for swollen hood and short upper glume, and a C. virgata spikelet for conspicuous distal fertile-lemma hair crown; retain hybrid uncertainty.
central_texas_lookalikes: Chloris cucullata: shorter more crowded raceme whorls, upper glume about 1–1.5 mm versus C. verticillata 2.8–3.5 mm; upper sterile lemma forms a distinctly rounded hood. Check an opened mature floret, not the overall head.
Chloris virgata: often annual, terminal feathery fan rather than separated whorls; conspicuous longer apical fertile-lemma hairs. Awn ranges overlap, so an awn length alone is insufficient.
Chloris andropogonoides: different long-arm architecture; inspect attachment levels and mature florets rather than calling all windmill-shaped heads C. verticillata.
Chloris × subdolichostachya: known hybrid/identity hold; do not assign hybrid or parent species from intermediate whorl spacing without specimen-level evidence.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: Long one-sided racemes in separated tiers
field_id_short_tiles.details: On ONE attached flowering culm, follow the central axis and locate approximately 10–16 one-sided racemes, often 5–15 cm long, arising in separated whorls; a solitary upright terminal raceme may remain. An entire ripe head can detach and tumble, so a loose head alone cannot prove where branches attached. Published measurements, not ruler readings from these images.
field_id_short_tiles.status: GROSS STRUCTURE VISIBLE; ATTACHED SAME-VOUCHER AXIS STILL NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · ROOTS AND TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Perennial fibrous tuft; lower nodes may root
field_id_short_tiles.details: Start with the real exposed fibrous-root crown (panel 6): clustered basal tillers, flattened lower shoots and bent stems establish a tufted perennial, NOT an underground rhizome. In living plants, prostrate/decumbent lower stem nodes can sometimes grow adventitious roots and allow a short spreading mat; the archived crown view does NOT prove any node along a creeping stem has rooted. To document that habit, follow ONE connected aboveground stem to a node with roots entering soil, then photograph the same stem and its original crown. Open the INNER blade–sheath junction for the actual shortly ciliate membranous ligule; FNA gives 0.7–1.3 mm and Kew GrassBase approximately 2 mm. The currently pictured pale collar hairs do NOT establish the membrane's free edge or its length.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ROOTED CROWN VISIBLE; ROOTING AT LOWER NODES AND TRUE LIGULE NOT PHOTOGRAPHICALLY PROVEN

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · ONE SPIKELET, TWO FLORETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Awns excluded from the spikelet-body length
field_id_short_tiles.details: Under 10–20×, isolate one mature laterally compressed spikelet, approximately 2–3.5 mm long WITHOUT the long awns. The lower floret is fertile/bisexual and the upper floret sterile. Attached raceme macros show awned units, but do not yet separate both florets and glumes on a calibrated dissection.
field_id_short_tiles.status: MACRO VISIBLE; COMPLETE SPIKELET DISSECTION MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · FIND BOTH GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.details: A mature spikelet has TWO basal glumes distinct from the awn-bearing lemmas. Published FNA values: lower glume about 2–3 mm, upper glume about 2.8–3.5 mm. Verify with a 1-mm ruler after separating the bracts; do not label an awn as arising from either glume. The upper-glume length helps distinguish the shorter-glumed hooded windmillgrass, but must not be used alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED MEASUREMENTS; GLUMES NOT SEPARATELY VERIFIED IN PIXELS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · TRACE TWO DIFFERENT AWNS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fertile lemma awn ≈4.8–9 mm; sterile ≈3.2–7 mm
field_id_short_tiles.details: The lower fertile lemma is approximately 2–3.5 mm long, three-veined, with a subapical awn about 4.8–9 mm. The UPPER sterile lemma is about 1.1–2.3 mm with its own awn around 3.2–7 mm. Both awns are lemma extensions, NOT glume awns. Count and measure them only after exposing their separate insertions; existing dry macros cannot prove which is which.
field_id_short_tiles.status: VISIBLE AWNS; ORIGIN AND MILLIMETER LENGTH NOT VERIFIED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · LOCAL LOOK-ALIKE CHECK
field_id_short_tiles.short: Hooded vs tumble: glume ≠ sterile hood
field_id_short_tiles.details: For hooded windmillgrass (Chloris cucullata), distinguish TWO different parts when dissecting: the short UPPER GLUME (about 1–1.5 mm in the Go Botany/FNA key) and the separately rounded/inflated UPPER STERILE FLORET (the 'hood', about 1–1.5 mm in GrassBase). Do NOT label that upper glume as the hood. C. cucullata also usually has shorter, more crowded head branches and short sterile-lemma awns (0–1.5 mm). Chloris virgata is typically annual with a terminal feathery set of branches and a conspicuous tuft of longer hairs near the fertile lemma tip. Chloris × subdolichostachya can be intermediate; tier spacing or an isolated awn cannot establish parentage. Keep a questionable plant as Chloris sp. until opened mature spikelets are compared.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COMPARISON TEACHABLE; MATCHED DISSECTED SPECIMENS MISSING
